paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between computational effort and loss for two different methods. The x-axis is labeled "TFLOPs" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.00 to 1.25 with tick marks at intervals of 0.25, on scale of 1e9. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and also uses a linear scale ranging from 2.40 to 2.75 with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. There are two lines on the plot: the first line is purple, has triangle markers, and is solid in style, representing the "Vanilla" method. It starts at approximately (0.10, 2.75) and ends at around (1.20, 2.5), showing a decreasing trend throughout. The second line is red, has circle markers, and is also solid, representing the "SepLLM" method. This line starts at approximately (0.10, 2.7) and ends at roughly (1.20, 2.48), also indicating a consistent decline across the x-axis. Throughout the graph red line is below the purple line. There's a gree dashed line along the x-axis at loss of 2.5, which intercepts the red line and ends at end of purple line, and is marked in a green star. From these intercepts, two other green dashed line, perpendicular to the x-axis is given, these lines are of height Loss 2.58. And between these two lines, at the top, a green line parallel the x-axis is there, and a text "1.28x" is given on top. A legend is given top right.
